chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Jackson's love of the organ and Fats teaching Basie
summary: Jackson played theater organs early in the morning; Fats taught Count Basie the organ in New York.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Right, that's right, you played the organ, too.
Oh, yeah. You know, I used to go early in the morning -- at some theaters we played with Calloway, I used to get permission to go early in the morning. Danny Barker used to follow me sometimes.
Yeah, a great guitarist, Danny Barker.

Uh-huh, and I used to go and get permission to play the organ before the theater opened early in the morning. I used to get there at seven o'clock, eight o'clock in the morning. That's how I hurt this ankle.
Count Basie had a great love for the organ also.

Fats taught him organ. Oh, yes, he'll tell you to this day that Fats started him out on the organ when he was in New York before he even went to Kansas City. You know, Basie and Elmer Williams come over here and hung out in New York together from over in Jersey.
Elmer Williams is a saxophone player?
That's right, that I told you was with Chick Webb.
Basie came over from Red Bank, I guess, huh?
That's right, and so did Elmer Williams.
Uh-huh, they used to come over and hang out together before they really got into the business.
